interest: This file offers a revealing look into wartime public interest and U.S. State Department handling of information concerning high-ranking Japanese naval officers. It illustrates how ordinary American citizens followed Pacific War developments and approached their elected representatives for information after Tokyo broadcast news of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto's death in late May 1943. Most notably, although U.S. military forces had intercepted and shot down Yamamoto's aircraft in April 1943 (Operation Vengeance) as a result of Magic signals intelligence, the State Department's official reply strictly cited Tokyo radio broadcasts and disclaimed responsibility for their accuracy, demonstrating the strict secrecy maintained around American codebreaking capabilities.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.321, covering commissioned officers of the Japanese Navy between November 1940 and May 1943) comprises two main components: a 1940 cross-reference sheet noting career details of Admiral Ryozo Nakamura from an Embassy Tokyo telegram, and a May 1943 constituent correspondence exchange initiated by Wisconsin resident George P. Kornely. Forwarded by Senator Alexander Wiley to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, Kornely's inquiry sought information regarding the death and funeral of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto. The Department of State, via Laurence E. Salisbury of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, replied with details derived exclusively from monitored Tokyo radio broadcasts reporting Yamamoto's death in an airplane, the honors bestowed by the Emperor, the transport of his ashes to Tokyo for a state funeral alongside Fleet Admiral Togo, and the appointment of Admiral Mineichi Koga as his successor.

subfiles.about: A Department of State cross-reference sheet indexing biographical data on Admiral Ryozo Nakamura from a 1940 diplomatic telegram from Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram 1205 dated November 26, 1940, sent by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Japan and filed under 711.94/1843. It records information supplied by the U.S. Naval Attaché concerning Admiral Ryozo Nakamura. The note highlights Nakamura's prior service as head of the Naval War College, Commander-in-Chief of the Second Fleet, and his retirement from the Supreme War Council.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet regarding Admiral Ryozo Nakamura

subfiles.about: A State Department letter providing public Tokyo radio broadcast information concerning the death, honors, and funeral of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto.
subfiles.summary: Writing for the Secretary of State, Laurence E. Salisbury responds to George P. Kornely's inquiry forwarded by Senator Alexander Wiley. The letter summarizes information obtained from Tokyo radio broadcasts regarding the death of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto in an airplane, posthumous imperial honors, the arrival of his ashes in Tokyo to lie in state at the Navy Club, his upcoming June 5 funeral alongside Admiral Togo, and the appointment of Admiral Mineichi Koga as his successor. Salisbury emphasizes that the State Department takes no responsibility for the accuracy of these Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Laurence E. Salisbury to George P. Kornely regarding Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto

subfiles.about: A transmittal letter from the Department of State to Senator Alexander Wiley enclosing its response to constituent George P. Kornely.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges Senator Alexander Wiley's letter of May 26, 1943, which forwarded George P. Kornely's inquiry about Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto. The letter encloses a copy of the Department's direct reply to Kornely for the Senator's records. In compliance with Senator Wiley's request, Kornely's original inquiry letter is returned.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Department of State to Senator Alexander Wiley transmitting reply to George P. Kornely

subfiles.about: A letter from Senator Alexander Wiley forwarding constituent George P. Kornely's inquiry regarding Admiral Yamamoto to Secretary of State Cordell Hull.
subfiles.summary: Senator Alexander Wiley of Wisconsin transmits a constituent letter from George P. Kornely of Two Rivers, Wisconsin, to Secretary of State Cordell Hull. Wiley asks the Department to reply directly to Mr. Kornely with whatever information is available concerning the death and burial of Japanese Admiral Yamamoto. He also requests the return of Kornely's letter for his Senate files once it has served its purpose.
subfiles.title: Letter from Senator Alexander Wiley to Secretary of State Cordell Hull forwarding constituent inquiry

subfiles.about: A constituent letter from Wisconsin citizen George P. Kornely to Senator Alexander Wiley requesting details on Admiral Yamamoto's death and burial.
subfiles.summary: George P. Kornely of Two Rivers, Wisconsin, writes to Senator Alexander Wiley asking for full details concerning the death and burial of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto of Japan. Although the copy bears the date May 23, 1942, internal context and official replies confirm it was sent on May 23, 1943, following Tokyo's public announcement of Yamamoto's death. This constituent inquiry initiated the subsequent State Department correspondence with Senator Wiley and Mr. Kornely.
subfiles.title: Letter from George P. Kornely to Senator Alexander Wiley inquiring about Admiral Yamamoto
